{"parentUuid":"7dc8da43-220b-475a-b81f-4da66d6c3269","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent (\"run this every Monday\", \"open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks\"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a \"remove once X\" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence (\"in 2 weeks\", \"every Monday\") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. Pairs with decompose-work (deterministic-vs-LLM split per approach) + capability-map (model × effort grounding) + promote-rule (consumes outcomes).\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- ccs:continue: Continue last CCS delegation session [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- ccs: Delegate task with intelligent profile selection [AUTO ENHANCE]\n- budget-check: /budget-check — Current Session Token Budget Status\n- devils-advocate: /devils-advocate — Adversarial Critique\n- drift-check: /drift-check — Run Drift Signals DR1-DR12\n- drill-me: /drill-me — Interactive Ubiquitous Language Extraction\n- grill-me: /grill-me — Relentless Plan/Design Interview\n- handoff-read: /handoff-read — Lightweight Last Session Load\n- master-plan: /master-plan — High-Level Work Decomposition\n- session-end: /session-end — Close Work Session\n- session-start: /session-start — Begin Work Session\n- session-verify: /session-verify — Mid-Session Alignment Check\n- spec-author: /spec-author — Create Dual-Layer Specification\n- spec-to-wiki: /spec-to-wiki — Convert Raw Spec to Obsidian Wiki Format\n- ul-audit: /ul-audit — Audit Ubiquitous Language Consistency\n- vbw-check: /vbw-check — Apply Verify-Before-Write Protocol\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch","skillCount":49,"isInitial":true},"type":"attachment","uuid":"d0ff2a89-8d38-48ca-8c2b-2bd575263729","timestamp":"2026-04-30T14:41:34.192Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"26da415a-76e5-4042-8420-5582125d8a7d","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"f4a8e03b-e443-4324-9ae1-57ee4504f28a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"87fb4cf9-997e-413f-9fe6-79f2b99bc3e9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011oSyF7s9g6Lzcv3E5Hn9mT","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# PROJECT CHARTER\n2\t## StockForge — Personal Investment Advisor for Vietnamese Stock Market\n3\t\n4\t> **Status**: Immutable v1.0 — changes require explicit charter revision.\n5\t> **Scope of immutability**: Vision, principles, success criteria.\n6\t> **Things that do evolve**: Agent configs, specs, implementation, signal weights, eval sets.\n7\t\n8\t---\n9\t\n10\t## Vision\n11\t\n12\tAn AI-first investment research and advisory system that combines **quant fund methodology** with **Vietnam-specific edge sources** (KOL networks, crowd sentiment, pump pattern detection) to surface high-conviction opportunities in an inefficient market where logic-based screening alone is insufficient.\n13\t\n14\tPrimary user: project owner (self) + 3-5 trusted peers in Vietnamese investing community.\n15\t\n16\tPrimary goal: build a system that compounds edge over time through proprietary data accumulation, not through any single clever algorithm. After 12-24 months of dogfood, the system should be a genuine advisor I would pay money for if someone else built it.\n17\t\n18\tNot a goal: high-frequency trading, replacing human judgment, becoming a SaaS in Year 1, beating frontier LLMs at general reasoning, providing licensed financial advice.\n19\t\n20\t---\n21\t\n22\t## The Core Insight (the why)\n23\t\n24\t**Quant funds (Renaissance, Two Sigma, DE Shaw) win in efficient markets through clean data + execution speed + diverse alpha factors.** They don't use sentiment from Facebook/YouTube because at their scale it's noise, not signal — and in efficient markets it gets arbitraged away anyway.\n25\t\n26\t**Vietnam stock market inverts this.** It is structurally inefficient:\n27\t- 85-90% retail investor share (vs 20-25% in US)\n28\t- Information asymmetry between sophisticated and retail crowd\n29\t- KOL/influencer recommendations measurably move prices\n30\t- \"Đội lái\" (pump operators) operate openly\n31\t- News and narrative cycles dominate over fundamentals for months at a time\n32\t- Foreign flow creates non-fundamental price pressure\n33\t\n34\tIn this market, **sentiment + influence + narrative tracking is signal, not noise**. And LLMs can process Vietnamese unstructured text at scale that was impossible before 2023.\n35\t\n36\tThis creates a **structural arbitrage**: apply quant methodology + LLM reasoning + sentiment/influence data layers that no commercial product offers for VN. Position not as \"decision maker\" but as **advisor + alert watcher + bias mirror**.\n37\t\n38\t---\n39\t\n40\t## The Craft Philosophy\n41\t\n42\tTake the craft seriously. Build for personal use first, commercial second.\n43\t\n44\t- Production-grade engineering standards from Day 1 (DDD + clean architecture + multi-loop discipline)\n45\t- Commercial extension kept as option, never as driver\n46\t- When self-use conflicts with hypothetical-future-SaaS, self-use wins\n47\t- Quality bar: I genuinely trust output enough to act on real money decisions\n48\t- Edge comes from compounding moats (proprietary data, calibration, personal bias log), not from any single feature\n49\t\n50\tReference models: Renaissance Technologies (data + iteration discipline), Bridgewater (principles-based decision making), personal Bloomberg Terminal (data density + analysis depth), Athletic.com (subscription-quality content for niche audience).\n51\t\n52\t---\n53\t\n54\t## Core Principles (non-negotiable)\n55\t\n56\t1. **Evidence grounding** — every claim, every number traceable to source + as-of date. Hallucination in finance = bug, not stylistic issue.\n57\t\n58\t2. **Structured output over narrative** — multi-criteria assessment, never single \"buy/sell\" score. Output is trade-off matrix.\n59\t\n60\t3. **Adversarial by design** — bear + bull + critic + quant + behavior + manager perspectives. Never consensus from single agent.\n61\t\n62\t4. **Proprietary data moat** — every news ingested, every KOL recommendation tracked, every thesis post-mortem'd compounds the edge. Raw data is sacred.\n63\t\n64\t5. **Pattern transfer + local adaptation** — global setups (cyclical bottom, dividend value, GARP) + Vietnam-specific overlays (policy timing, foreign flow, narrative phase).\n65\t\n66\t6. **Human-in-loop is the product** — augment thinking, never replace it. System should challenge user's gut instinct without overriding it.\n67\t\n68\t7. **Dogfood mandatory** — if I don't use it weekly for real decisions, the feature gets killed. Self-use is the only validation that matters in Year 1.\n69\t\n70\t8. **Calibration over confidence** — system tracks its own accuracy across signal types, never claims confidence it hasn't earned through hit rate.\n71\t\n72\t9. **No LLM math** — LLM never generates numbers. All calculations through deterministic code with verified data inputs. LLM only interprets.\n73\t\n74\t10. **Position sizing & risk management are deterministic** — code-enforced rules, LLM cannot override. Maximum position size, sector concentration, stop loss rules are immutable per session.\n75\t\n76\t---\n77\t\n78\t## The Four-Tier Signal Architecture\n79\t\n80\tSystem operates on four distinct signal tiers, each with different lead time, reliability, and processing approach:\n81\t\n82\t**Tier 1 — Hard Data (deterministic):** prices, volumes, fundamentals, foreign flow, macro indicators. Zero LLM, pure code. Lead time: hours-days.\n83\t\n84\t**Tier 2 — Official Narrative (semi-structured):** mainstream financial news, broker reports, official company disclosures, government announcements. LLM extracts claims + classifies sentiment + detects contradictions. Lead time: real-time.\n85\t\n86\t**Tier 3 — Influence Network (semi-structured):** YouTube channels, Facebook KOL pages, Telegram channels, podcasts. LLM transcribes + extracts recommendations + tags entities. Calibration database tracks each KOL's accuracy over time. Lead time: can lead by days.\n87\t\n88\t**Tier 4 — Crowd Sentiment & Pump Detection (unstructured):** community forums, public chat groups, comments. LLM classifies sentiment + detects coordinated posting + identifies pump narratives + tracks narrative lifecycle phase. Lead time: typically lags price (signals exhaustion).\n89\t\n90\tThe combination — when Tier 1+2+3 agree before Tier 4 heats up = early opportunity; when Tier 4 hot but Tier 1+2 don't support = likely top — is the core analytical edge.\n91\t\n92\tSee `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` for detailed tier specs.\n93\t\n94\t---\n95\t\n96\t## First Sub-Scope (locked 6 months)\n97\t\n98\t**Vietnam stocks listed on HOSE/HNX/UPCoM**, specifically:\n99\t- VN30 + mid-cap (vốn hóa 2,000-50,000 tỷ VND) for primary coverage\n100\t- Long-only equity strategies (no derivatives, no shorting)\n101\t- Holding periods: 1-month minimum, 6-24 month preferred\n102\t- Position sizing per stock: 5-15% of portfolio\n103\t\n104\tOut of scope (Year 1): derivatives, warrants (CW), short selling, cryptocurrency, fund products, foreign markets, day trading, automated execution.\n105\t\n106\t---\n107\t\n108\t## Honest Boundaries (what system does NOT do)\n109\t\n110\t- **Predict price** — system predicts narrative phase, money flow direction, mispricing level. Never a price target with false precision.\n111\t- **Replace fundamental research** — surfaces opportunities, user must verify thesis before acting.\n112\t- **Execute trades** — pure research/alert tool. Execution stays manual.\n113\t- **Provide licensed financial advice** — personal research aid only. Output explicitly framed as \"thesis exploration\", not \"buy/sell recommendation\".\n114\t- **Time the market precisely** — works on phase identification (early/mid/late), not on tick-level timing.\n115\t- **Insider information** — uses only public sources. No paid leaks, no insider channels, no anything that crosses legal/ethical lines.\n116\t\n117\t---\n118\t\n119\t## Success Criteria\n120\t\n121\t**Month 3 (end of Phase 1 — Foundation):**\n122\t- Tier 1 + 2 data pipeline operational for VN30\n123\t- 50 companies have basic dossier in wiki\n124\t- First 5 thesis recorded with formal structure\n125\t- Can run /thesis-validate on a stock end-to-end in <5 minutes\n126\t\n127\t**Month 6 (end of Phase 2 — Edge Sources):**\n128\t- 30+ KOL channels tracked, calibration database has >100 recommendations with outcomes pending\n129\t- Tier 3 + 4 ingestion operational for top 100 stocks\n130\t- First detectable pump pattern caught (warning issued before public dump)\n131\t- 20+ thesis logged, first 5 hit 3-month review\n132\t\n133\t**Month 9 (end of Phase 3 — Multi-perspective):**\n134\t- Bear/bull/critic/quant/macro/behavior agents operational\n135\t- Pattern library has 15+ Vietnam-specific patterns with outcome data\n136\t- Personal bias log shows 3+ identified biases\n137\t- Thesis hit rate measurable (statistically meaningful sample)\n138\t\n139\t**Month 12 (end of Phase 4 — Compounding):**\n140\t- Karpathy outer loop optimizing signal weights weekly\n141\t- Cross-validation: system suggestions vs my manual analysis = where do they diverge?\n142\t- 3-5 trusted peers using it, providing feedback\n143\t- Demonstrable alpha vs VN-Index on dogfood portfolio (or honest accounting of why not)\n144\t\n145\t**Ultimate signal of success**: When my gut says \"buy XYZ\", I check what StockForge says first — and seriously consider it when it disagrees.\n146\t\n147\t---\n148\t\n149\t## Technical Foundation (locked Phase 1-3)\n150\t\n151\t**Stack:**\n152\t- **Python primary** — for data science, LLM workflows, time-series, backtesting (heavier than IdeaForge which was TS-primary)\n153\t- **Postgres 16 + TimescaleDB + pgvector + pg_trgm** — single DB for time-series + relational + vector\n154\t- **Redis** — cache + pub/sub + queue broker\n155\t- **Cloudflare R2** — raw content storage (PDFs, transcripts, scraped pages)\n156\t- **Claude API primary** — Sonnet for most tasks, Opus for thesis synthesis\n157\t- **OpenAI embeddings** — text-embedding-3-small (Vietnamese acceptable)\n158\t- **NestJS** — only if/when we need a public-facing API (Phase 4+)\n159\t- **Streamlit/Next.js** — Streamlit for personal dashboard (Phase 1-2), Next.js if SaaS path\n160\t- **Apache Airflow / Prefect** — data pipeline orchestration\n161\t\n162\t**Architecture:**\n163\t- Clean Architecture with DDD tactical patterns (same as IdeaForge)\n164\t- 9 bounded contexts (see `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`)\n165\t- Event-driven for cross-context communication\n166\t- Multi-loop execution (Karpathy outer + Continuous middle + Per-stock inner)\n167\t\n168\t**Development approach:**\n169\t- AI-first: Claude Code as primary builder, human as spec author + reviewer + bias-checker\n170\t- Spec-Driven (SDD) + Domain-Driven (DDD) + selective BDD\n171\t- Sandwich pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier) from Day 1\n172\t- Verify-Before-Write (VBW) protocol mandatory\n173\t- Three-tier quality gates (deterministic / probabilistic / human)\n174\t\n175\t---\n176\t\n177\t## Data Sources (Tier 1 budget)\n178\t\n179\t**Free/cheap (Phase 1):**\n180\t- vnstock (open source) — historical EOD, fundamentals\n181\t- Vietstock public — financial reports\n182\t- TCBS API — semi-public market data\n183\t- CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz — news scraping\n184\t- Public YouTube channels — transcript via yt-dlp + Whisper\n185\t- Public Facebook fanpages — selective scraping (legal grey, careful scope)\n186\t\n187\t**Paid (Phase 2-3 if budget allows):**\n188\t- FiinPro Platform — comprehensive fundamental data (~30-100M VND/year)\n189\t- Wichart — pre-cleaned data\n190\t- SSI FastConnect — realtime quotes if needed\n191\t\n192\t**Budget cap Year 1**: 50M VND for data + LLM combined.\n193\t\n194\t---\n195\t\n196\t## Meta-Discipline\n197\t\n198\tThese charter principles override daily decisions:\n199\t\n200\t- **When in doubt, simplify** — minimum code that solves the problem, nothing speculative\n201\t- **Ship thin slices, not perfect systems** — each phase ends with something I actually use\n202\t- **Document what you learn, not what you plan** — post-mortem > prospective docs\n203\t- **Dogfood or delete** — features I don't use weekly get removed\n204\t- **Calibrate, don't guess** — every confidence claim must have outcome tracking\n205\t- **Stay agnostic about commercial outcome** — build for the craft, not for the exit\n206\t\n207\t---\n208\t\n209\t## Revision Protocol\n210\t\n211\tThis charter changes only when:\n212\t- A core principle proves materially wrong through 30+ hours of real use\n213\t- Scope demonstrably needs revision based on accumulated dogfood data\n214\t- Technical foundation invalidated by external event (tool deprecation, regulatory change, etc.)\n215\t\n216\tCharter revisions require:\n217\t- Written rationale with evidence (linked to specific sessions/post-mortems)\n218\t- 48-hour cool-down before committing change\n219\t- Explicit version bump (v1.0 → v2.0)\n220\t\n221\tMinor clarifications go in `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`. This charter stays stable.\n222\t\n223\t---\n224\t\n225\t## Document Index\n226\t\n227\t| Document | Purpose | Stability |\n228\t|---|---|---|\n229\t| `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` (this) | Vision + principles | Immutable for ~3 months |\n230\t| `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` | Agent configs, skills, workflows | Living, frequent updates |\n231\t| `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` | How to write specs | Stable |\n232\t| `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` | Strategic: signal architecture | Stable |\n233\t| `specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md` | First implementation spec | Stable |\n234\t| `specs/tier2-feature/002-influence-network-tracking.md` | KOL tracking system spec | Stable |\n235\t| `specs/tier2-feature/003-crowd-sentiment-pump-detection.md` | Pump detection spec | Stable |\n236\t| `specs/tier2-feature/004-multi-perspective-adversarial-agents.md` | Adversarial analysis spec | Stable |\n237\t| `specs/tier2-feature/005-karpathy-outer-loop.md` | Pipeline self-optimization spec | Stable |\n238\t| `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` | Current state | Continuously updated |\n239\t| `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules | Append-mostly |\n240\t| `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/` | All thesis ever recorded | Append-only |\n241\t| `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/` | Thesis outcome reviews | Append-only |\n242\t| `agent-workspace/calibration/` | KOL accuracy, signal calibration data | Continuously updated |\n243\t\n244\t---\n245\t\n246\t## Anti-Charter (what we explicitly reject)\n247\t\n248\tTo stay focused, we reject these tempting paths:\n249\t\n250\t- **Predict prices with ML models** — models trained on VN price data overfit; no edge there.\n251\t- **Compete with broker research** — we have less data, less staff. We win on integration + edge sources, not on raw analysis depth.\n252\t- **Build for general retail public** — we build for ourselves and 3-5 peers. Mass market needs hand-holding we won't provide.\n253\t- **Trust LLM for numbers** — every numerical output must come from code with traceable inputs.\n254\t- **Build features without dogfooding** — speculative features die fast in this project.\n255\t- **Optimize for backtest performance** — Goodhart's Law is real. We optimize for forward decision quality.\n256\t- **Make money fast** — this is a 24-month project minimum to reach edge. Quick wins are anti-pattern.\n257\t"}]},"uuid":"8ba7888a-bb3b-4ea4-bb9d-8bfa64bf0031","timestamp":"2026-04-30T14:41:44.365Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\PROJECT_CHARTER.md","content":"# PROJECT CHARTER\n## StockForge — Personal Investment Advisor for Vietnamese Stock Market\n\n> **Status**: Immutable v1.0 — changes require explicit charter revision.\n> **Scope of immutability**: Vision, principles, success criteria.\n> **Things that do evolve**: Agent configs, specs, implementation, signal weights, eval sets.\n\n---\n\n## Vision\n\nAn AI-first investment research and advisory system that combines **quant fund methodology** with **Vietnam-specific edge sources** (KOL networks, crowd sentiment, pump pattern detection) to surface high-conviction opportunities in an inefficient market where logic-based screening alone is insufficient.\n\nPrimary user: project owner (self) + 3-5 trusted peers in Vietnamese investing community.\n\nPrimary goal: build a system that compounds edge over time through proprietary data accumulation, not through any single clever algorithm. After 12-24 months of dogfood, the system should be a genuine advisor I would pay money for if someone else built it.\n\nNot a goal: high-frequency trading, replacing human judgment, becoming a SaaS in Year 1, beating frontier LLMs at general reasoning, providing licensed financial advice.\n\n---\n\n## The Core Insight (the why)\n\n**Quant funds (Renaissance, Two Sigma, DE Shaw) win in efficient markets through clean data + execution speed + diverse alpha factors.** They don't use sentiment from Facebook/YouTube because at their scale it's noise, not signal — and in efficient markets it gets arbitraged away anyway.\n\n**Vietnam stock market inverts this.** It is structurally inefficient:\n- 85-90% retail investor share (vs 20-25% in US)\n- Information asymmetry between sophisticated and retail crowd\n- KOL/influencer recommendations measurably move prices\n- \"Đội lái\" (pump operators) operate openly\n- News and narrative cycles dominate over fundamentals for months at a time\n- Foreign flow creates non-fundamental price pressure\n\nIn this market, **sentiment + influence + narrative tracking is signal, not noise**. And LLMs can process Vietnamese unstructured text at scale that was impossible before 2023.\n\nThis creates a **structural arbitrage**: apply quant methodology + LLM reasoning + sentiment/influence data layers that no commercial product offers for VN. Position not as \"decision maker\" but as **advisor + alert watcher + bias mirror**.\n\n---\n\n## The Craft Philosophy\n\nTake the craft seriously. Build for personal use first, commercial second.\n\n- Production-grade engineering standards from Day 1 (DDD + clean architecture + multi-loop discipline)\n- Commercial extension kept as option, never as driver\n- When self-use conflicts with hypothetical-future-SaaS, self-use wins\n- Quality bar: I genuinely trust output enough to act on real money decisions\n- Edge comes from compounding moats (proprietary data, calibration, personal bias log), not from any single feature\n\nReference models: Renaissance Technologies (data + iteration discipline), Bridgewater (principles-based decision making), personal Bloomberg Terminal (data density + analysis depth), Athletic.com (subscription-quality content for niche audience).\n\n---\n\n## Core Principles (non-negotiable)\n\n1. **Evidence grounding** — every claim, every number traceable to source + as-of date. Hallucination in finance = bug, not stylistic issue.\n\n2. **Structured output over narrative** — multi-criteria assessment, never single \"buy/sell\" score. Output is trade-off matrix.\n\n3. **Adversarial by design** — bear + bull + critic + quant + behavior + manager perspectives. Never consensus from single agent.\n\n4. **Proprietary data moat** — every news ingested, every KOL recommendation tracked, every thesis post-mortem'd compounds the edge. Raw data is sacred.\n\n5. **Pattern transfer + local adaptation** — global setups (cyclical bottom, dividend value, GARP) + Vietnam-specific overlays (policy timing, foreign flow, narrative phase).\n\n6. **Human-in-loop is the product** — augment thinking, never replace it. System should challenge user's gut instinct without overriding it.\n\n7. **Dogfood mandatory** — if I don't use it weekly for real decisions, the feature gets killed. Self-use is the only validation that matters in Year 1.\n\n8. **Calibration over confidence** — system tracks its own accuracy across signal types, never claims confidence it hasn't earned through hit rate.\n\n9. **No LLM math** — LLM never generates numbers. All calculations through deterministic code with verified data inputs. LLM only interprets.\n\n10. **Position sizing & risk management are deterministic** — code-enforced rules, LLM cannot override. Maximum position size, sector concentration, stop loss rules are immutable per session.\n\n---\n\n## The Four-Tier Signal Architecture\n\nSystem operates on four distinct signal tiers, each with different lead time, reliability, and processing approach:\n\n**Tier 1 — Hard Data (deterministic):** prices, volumes, fundamentals, foreign flow, macro indicators. Zero LLM, pure code. Lead time: hours-days.\n\n**Tier 2 — Official Narrative (semi-structured):** mainstream financial news, broker reports, official company disclosures, government announcements. LLM extracts claims + classifies sentiment + detects contradictions. Lead time: real-time.\n\n**Tier 3 — Influence Network (semi-structured):** YouTube channels, Facebook KOL pages, Telegram channels, podcasts. LLM transcribes + extracts recommendations + tags entities. Calibration database tracks each KOL's accuracy over time. Lead time: can lead by days.\n\n**Tier 4 — Crowd Sentiment & Pump Detection (unstructured):** community forums, public chat groups, comments. LLM classifies sentiment + detects coordinated posting + identifies pump narratives + tracks narrative lifecycle phase. Lead time: typically lags price (signals exhaustion).\n\nThe combination — when Tier 1+2+3 agree before Tier 4 heats up = early opportunity; when Tier 4 hot but Tier 1+2 don't support = likely top — is the core analytical edge.\n\nSee `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` for detailed tier specs.\n\n---\n\n## First Sub-Scope (locked 6 months)\n\n**Vietnam stocks listed on HOSE/HNX/UPCoM**, specifically:\n- VN30 + mid-cap (vốn hóa 2,000-50,000 tỷ VND) for primary coverage\n- Long-only equity strategies (no derivatives, no shorting)\n- Holding periods: 1-month minimum, 6-24 month preferred\n- Position sizing per stock: 5-15% of portfolio\n\nOut of scope (Year 1): derivatives, warrants (CW), short selling, cryptocurrency, fund products, foreign markets, day trading, automated execution.\n\n---\n\n## Honest Boundaries (what system does NOT do)\n\n- **Predict price** — system predicts narrative phase, money flow direction, mispricing level. Never a price target with false precision.\n- **Replace fundamental research** — surfaces opportunities, user must verify thesis before acting.\n- **Execute trades** — pure research/alert tool. Execution stays manual.\n- **Provide licensed financial advice** — personal research aid only. Output explicitly framed as \"thesis exploration\", not \"buy/sell recommendation\".\n- **Time the market precisely** — works on phase identification (early/mid/late), not on tick-level timing.\n- **Insider information** — uses only public sources. No paid leaks, no insider channels, no anything that crosses legal/ethical lines.\n\n---\n\n## Success Criteria\n\n**Month 3 (end of Phase 1 — Foundation):**\n- Tier 1 + 2 data pipeline operational for VN30\n- 50 companies have basic dossier in wiki\n- First 5 thesis recorded with formal structure\n- Can run /thesis-validate on a stock end-to-end in <5 minutes\n\n**Month 6 (end of Phase 2 — Edge Sources):**\n- 30+ KOL channels tracked, calibration database has >100 recommendations with outcomes pending\n- Tier 3 + 4 ingestion operational for top 100 stocks\n- First detectable pump pattern caught (warning issued before public dump)\n- 20+ thesis logged, first 5 hit 3-month review\n\n**Month 9 (end of Phase 3 — Multi-perspective):**\n- Bear/bull/critic/quant/macro/behavior agents operational\n- Pattern library has 15+ Vietnam-specific patterns with outcome data\n- Personal bias log shows 3+ identified biases\n- Thesis hit rate measurable (statistically meaningful sample)\n\n**Month 12 (end of Phase 4 — Compounding):**\n- Karpathy outer loop optimizing signal weights weekly\n- Cross-validation: system suggestions vs my manual analysis = where do they diverge?\n- 3-5 trusted peers using it, providing feedback\n- Demonstrable alpha vs VN-Index on dogfood portfolio (or honest accounting of why not)\n\n**Ultimate signal of success**: When my gut says \"buy XYZ\", I check what StockForge says first — and seriously consider it when it disagrees.\n\n---\n\n## Technical Foundation (locked Phase 1-3)\n\n**Stack:**\n- **Python primary** — for data science, LLM workflows, time-series, backtesting (heavier than IdeaForge which was TS-primary)\n- **Postgres 16 + TimescaleDB + pgvector + pg_trgm** — single DB for time-series + relational + vector\n- **Redis** — cache + pub/sub + queue broker\n- **Cloudflare R2** — raw content storage (PDFs, transcripts, scraped pages)\n- **Claude API primary** — Sonnet for most tasks, Opus for thesis synthesis\n- **OpenAI embeddings** — text-embedding-3-small (Vietnamese acceptable)\n- **NestJS** — only if/when we need a public-facing API (Phase 4+)\n- **Streamlit/Next.js** — Streamlit for personal dashboard (Phase 1-2), Next.js if SaaS path\n- **Apache Airflow / Prefect** — data pipeline orchestration\n\n**Architecture:**\n- Clean Architecture with DDD tactical patterns (same as IdeaForge)\n- 9 bounded contexts (see `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`)\n- Event-driven for cross-context communication\n- Multi-loop execution (Karpathy outer + Continuous middle + Per-stock inner)\n\n**Development approach:**\n- AI-first: Claude Code as primary builder, human as spec author + reviewer + bias-checker\n- Spec-Driven (SDD) + Domain-Driven (DDD) + selective BDD\n- Sandwich pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier) from Day 1\n- Verify-Before-Write (VBW) protocol mandatory\n- Three-tier quality gates (deterministic / probabilistic / human)\n\n---\n\n## Data Sources (Tier 1 budget)\n\n**Free/cheap (Phase 1):**\n- vnstock (open source) — historical EOD, fundamentals\n- Vietstock public — financial reports\n- TCBS API — semi-public market data\n- CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz — news scraping\n- Public YouTube channels — transcript via yt-dlp + Whisper\n- Public Facebook fanpages — selective scraping (legal grey, careful scope)\n\n**Paid (Phase 2-3 if budget allows):**\n- FiinPro Platform — comprehensive fundamental data (~30-100M VND/year)\n- Wichart — pre-cleaned data\n- SSI FastConnect — realtime quotes if needed\n\n**Budget cap Year 1**: 50M VND for data + LLM combined.\n\n---\n\n## Meta-Discipline\n\nThese charter principles override daily decisions:\n\n- **When in doubt, simplify** — minimum code that solves the problem, nothing speculative\n- **Ship thin slices, not perfect systems** — each phase ends with something I actually use\n- **Document what you learn, not what you plan** — post-mortem > prospective docs\n- **Dogfood or delete** — features I don't use weekly get removed\n- **Calibrate, don't guess** — every confidence claim must have outcome tracking\n- **Stay agnostic about commercial outcome** — build for the craft, not for the exit\n\n---\n\n## Revision Protocol\n\nThis charter changes only when:\n- A core principle proves materially wrong through 30+ hours of real use\n- Scope demonstrably needs revision based on accumulated dogfood data\n- Technical foundation invalidated by external event (tool deprecation, regulatory change, etc.)\n\nCharter revisions require:\n- Written rationale with evidence (linked to specific sessions/post-mortems)\n- 48-hour cool-down before committing change\n- Explicit version bump (v1.0 → v2.0)\n\nMinor clarifications go in `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`. This charter stays stable.\n\n---\n\n## Document Index\n\n| Document | Purpose | Stability |\n|---|---|---|\n| `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` (this) | Vision + principles | Immutable for ~3 months |\n| `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` | Agent configs, skills, workflows | Living, frequent updates |\n| `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` | How to write specs | Stable |\n| `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` | Strategic: signal architecture | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md` | First implementation spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/002-influence-network-tracking.md` | KOL tracking system spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/003-crowd-sentiment-pump-detection.md` | Pump detection spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/004-multi-perspective-adversarial-agents.md` | Adversarial analysis spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/005-karpathy-outer-loop.md` | Pipeline self-optimization spec | Stable |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` | Current state | Continuously updated |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules | Append-mostly |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/` | All thesis ever recorded | Append-only |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/` | Thesis outcome reviews | Append-only |\n| `agent-workspace/calibration/` | KOL accuracy, signal calibration data | Continuously updated |\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Charter (what we explicitly reject)\n\nTo stay focused, we reject these tempting paths:\n\n- **Predict prices with ML models** — models trained on VN price data overfit; no edge there.\n- **Compete with broker research** — we have less data, less staff. We win on integration + edge sources, not on raw analysis depth.\n- **Build for general retail public** — we build for ourselves and 3-5 peers. Mass market needs hand-holding we won't provide.\n- **Trust LLM for numbers** — every numerical output must come from code with traceable inputs.\n- **Build features without dogfooding** — speculative features die fast in this project.\n- **Optimize for backtest performance** — Goodhart's Law is real. We optimize for forward decision quality.\n- **Make money fast** — this is a 24-month project minimum to reach edge. Quick wins are anti-pattern.\n","numLines":257,"startLine":1,"totalLines":257}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f4a8e03b-e443-4324-9ae1-57ee4504f28a","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"26da415a-76e5-4042-8420-5582125d8a7d","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"54a3615e-06c7-4bd1-8823-15ab67cf8f5e","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"87fb4cf9-997e-413f-9fe6-79f2b99bc3e9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PuY87DkyHgnfhmZfHTBBsU","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Financial Data Protocol — StockForge\n2\t\n3\t> Stock-specific data integrity rules. Real money depends on these.\n4\t> Companion to `invariants.md`. Read both before working with any data layer.\n5\t\n6\t## Why This Exists\n7\t\n8\tStock data has unique failure modes that don't exist in idea-validation or general SaaS:\n9\t- **Look-ahead bias** — using data agent didn't have at decision time → fake \"winning\" backtest\n10\t- **Survivorship bias** — only training on companies still trading → models that fail on real future\n11\t- **Adjustment confusion** — comparing pre-split price to post-split → 10x errors\n12\t- **Stale fundamentals** — using FY2023 filed in March 2024 for January 2024 decision → impossible-in-reality\n13\t- **Currency drift** — FX changes between price update and conversion → silent value distortion\n14\t- **Source disagreement** — vnstock vs FiinPro vs TCBS disagree → which to trust?\n15\t\n16\tThis protocol is the answer to each.\n17\t\n18\t---\n19\t\n20\t## Rule 1: Point-in-Time Integrity\n21\t\n22\t### The Problem\n23\t\n24\tYou query \"what was company X's P/E on 2023-06-15?\" The naive answer uses Q1 2023 EPS. But Q1 2023 was filed on 2023-04-30 — was it really known on April 30, or April 28? When did ratios get computed? Different sources have different filing dates for the same period.\n25\t\n26\t### The Rule\n27\t\n28\tEvery fundamental data record has THREE date fields:\n29\t- `period_end` — what period this represents (e.g., 2023-03-31 for Q1 2023)\n30\t- `filing_date` — when this was officially published\n31\t- `ingested_at` — when our system learned about it\n32\t\n33\tFor backtest: filter `WHERE filing_date <= as_of_date AND ingested_at <= as_of_date`.\n34\tFor live: filter `WHERE filing_date IS NOT NULL` (no in-progress estimates).\n35\tFor estimates/forecasts: separate table `forecasts` with `forecast_date`, `for_period_end`, `source`.\n36\t\n37\t### The Enforcement\n38\t\n39\t`FundamentalRepository` has only two methods:\n40\t- `get_as_of(ticker, as_of_date)` — uses point-in-time filter\n41\t- `get_latest(ticker)` — uses today's date\n42\t\n43\tThere is no `get_all()` or `get_by_period()` that could be misused for backtest.\n44\t\n45\t---\n46\t\n47\t## Rule 2: Survivorship-Aware Universe Construction\n48\t\n49\t### The Problem\n50\t\n51\tIf you backtest \"buy stocks with P/E < 10 in 2018, hold 3 years\", and your dataset only includes companies still listed in 2024, you've cherry-picked survivors. Real 2018 universe included companies that later went bankrupt or got delisted.\n52\t\n53\t### The Rule\n54\t\n55\t- Universe table includes ALL stocks ever traded, with `first_traded_at`, `delisted_at`, `suspended_periods`\n56\t- Backtest universe construction: `WHERE first_traded_at <= as_of_date AND (delisted_at IS NULL OR delisted_at > as_of_date) AND NOT in_suspension(ticker, as_of_date)`\n57\t- Delisted stocks keep their full price history\n58\t- \"Why delisted\" tagged: `BANKRUPTCY | MERGER | PRIVATIZATION | EXCHANGE_MIGRATION | OTHER`\n59\t\n60\t### The Enforcement\n61\t\n62\tBacktest framework `Universe.construct(as_of_date)` returns the survivor-aware universe. There is no `Universe.current_listed_only()` method available in backtest paths.\n63\t\n64\tCI gate checks: backtest dataset must include at least 5% delisted stocks. Less = warning that dataset is suspect.\n65\t\n66\t---\n67\t\n68\t## Rule 3: Adjustment Type Tagging\n69\t\n70\t### The Problem\n71\t\n72\tStock at 100,000 splits 1:2 → next day at 50,000. If you look at raw historical data, looks like 50% loss. Adjusted data smooths this out, but mixing adjusted (for chart) with unadjusted (for transaction calculation) gives 10x errors.\n73\t\n74\t### The Rule\n75\t\n76\tEvery price record has `adjustment_type`:\n77\t- `NONE` — raw historical (what you actually paid)\n78\t- `DIVIDEND` — adjusted for dividends only\n79\t- `SPLIT` — adjusted for splits only\n80\t- `BOTH` — fully adjusted (typical for charts/return calc)\n81\t\n82\t`Quote` value object has `adjustment_type` field. Repository methods are explicit:\n83\t- `get_quotes_adjusted(ticker, range)` → returns BOTH\n84\t- `get_quotes_raw(ticker, range)` → returns NONE\n85\t- No mixed query allowed.\n86\t\n87\t### The Enforcement\n88\t\n89\tQuote dataclass enforces `adjustment_type` not None. Mixing in same calculation raises `MixedAdjustmentError`.\n90\t\n91\t---\n92\t\n93\t## Rule 4: Source Attribution & Reconciliation\n94\t\n95\t### The Problem\n96\t\n97\tvnstock says HPG Q3 2024 revenue = 35,000 tỷ. FiinPro says 35,200 tỷ. TCBS says 34,800 tỷ. Which is \"true\"?\n98\t\n99\t### The Rule\n100\t\n101\t- Every data point stores `source_provider` (enum: VNSTOCK | FIINPRO | TCBS | SSI | MANUAL | SCRAPED_<source>)\n102\t- \"Truth\" view materialized via reconciliation rules:\n103\t  - If only one source: that's the truth\n104\t  - If sources agree (within 1% tolerance): truth = average, confidence = HIGH\n105\t  - If sources disagree (>1%): truth = manual override OR flag for review, confidence = LOW\n106\t  - Manual override always wins, with `override_reason` documented\n107\t- UI shows truth value + \"X of Y sources confirm\" badge\n108\t\n109\t### The Enforcement\n110\t\n111\t`ReconciledFundamental` view in DB. Application layer queries reconciled view by default. Raw single-source queries explicitly via `RawFundamentalRepository` for debugging only.\n112\t\n113\t---\n114\t\n115\t## Rule 5: Currency Discipline\n116\t\n117\t### The Problem\n118\t\n119\tVND fundamentals + USD foreign comparable + EUR debt instrument = silent type confusion if not strict.\n120\t\n121\t### The Rule\n122\t\n123\t- `Money` value object always has `currency` field (default VND for domestic data)\n124\t- Cross-currency math requires explicit `convert(target_currency, as_of_rate)` call\n125\t- FX rates stored with `as_of_date` (point-in-time integrity applies)\n126\t- No implicit conversion — `Money(100, USD) + Money(2_000_000, VND)` raises `CurrencyMismatchError`\n127\t\n128\t### The Enforcement\n129\t\n130\t`Money` dataclass `__add__`, `__sub__`, `__mul__` validate currency. CI test verifies no implicit conversion possible.\n131\t\n132\t---\n133\t\n134\t## Rule 6: LLM Output Provenance\n135\t\n136\t### The Problem\n137\t\n138\tLLM extracts \"HPG announced 30% dividend increase\" from a news article. Two months later, you wonder: was that real or hallucinated?\n139\t\n140\t### The Rule\n141\t\n142\tEvery LLM-extracted claim record has:\n143\t- `source_url` — where extracted from (URL or file path)\n144\t- `source_text_excerpt` — exact text quoted (≤500 chars)\n145\t- `extractor_model` — model name + version (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\")\n146\t- `extractor_prompt_hash` — hash of system prompt used (for reproducibility)\n147\t- `extractor_version` — code version (commit hash)\n148\t- `extracted_at` — timestamp\n149\t- `confidence_extracted` — LLM's stated confidence in the extraction (0-1)\n150\t- `verified_by_human` — bool (default false)\n151\t\n152\tWithout all these fields, claim cannot be inserted to DB.\n153\t\n154\t### The Enforcement\n155\t\n156\tRepository constructor validates all fields. Schema NOT NULL constraints. Verifier agent randomly samples 5% of new claims for human review queue.\n157\t\n158\t---\n159\t\n160\t## Rule 7: Sentiment Score Calibration\n161\t\n162\t### The Problem\n163\t\n164\tLLM says \"this article is 80% bullish\". What does 80% mean? Is it calibrated to anything?\n165\t\n166\t### The Rule\n167\t\n168\tSentiment scores are categorical, not numeric:\n169\t- `STRONGLY_BULLISH | BULLISH | NEUTRAL | BEARISH | STRONGLY_BEARISH`\n170\t\n171\tPlus extracted features:\n172\t- `mentioned_tickers: list[Ticker]`\n173\t- `key_phrases: list[str]`\n174\t- `tone_indicators: list[str]` (e.g., \"uses superlatives\", \"compares to leader\", \"raises concern\")\n175\t\n176\tAggregation to \"sentiment score\" happens in code, not LLM:\n177\t- e.g., `sentiment_score = (bullish_count - bearish_count) / total_count` over a time window\n178\t\n179\t### The Enforcement\n180\t\n181\tSentiment LLM tasks return enum, not number. Application layer converts to score with explicit formula. Backtest can validate which scoring formula correlates with subsequent price moves.\n182\t\n183\t---\n184\t\n185\t## Rule 8: Anti-Look-Ahead in News & Sentiment\n186\t\n187\t### The Problem\n188\t\n189\tYou backtest \"buy stocks with positive news momentum\". But the news article from Jan 15 might have been published 8pm — too late to act. Or the sentiment was scored 3 days later when more context was available.\n190\t\n191\t### The Rule\n192\t\n193\tEvery news/sentiment record has:\n194\t- `published_at` — when source published it (best estimate)\n195\t- `ingested_at` — when our system saw it\n196\t- `scored_at` — when sentiment was computed\n197\t\n198\tBacktest filters: `WHERE published_at <= as_of_date AND scored_at <= as_of_date AND published_at + acting_lag <= action_date`\n199\t\n200\tWhere `acting_lag` = realistic time between news and possible trade (e.g., next day open if published after market close).\n201\t\n202\t### The Enforcement\n203\t\n204\tNews/sentiment repository has only `get_known_as_of(ticker, as_of_date)` method for backtest. The lag is enforced in the query.\n205\t\n206\t---\n207\t\n208\t## Rule 9: KOL Recommendation Provenance\n209\t\n210\t### The Problem\n211\t\n212\tKOL says \"buy HPG\" in a 30-minute video. When exactly? Was it part of a long disclaimer? Was it conditional (\"if breaks 30k then buy\")?\n213\t\n214\t### The Rule\n215\t\n216\tExtracted KOL recommendations include:\n217\t- `source_url` — full video/post URL\n218\t- `timestamp_in_source` — for video: timestamp range (e.g., \"12:34-13:02\")\n219\t- `transcript_excerpt` — exact text quoted\n220\t- `extracted_intent` — categorical: STRONG_BUY | BUY | WATCH | NEUTRAL | AVOID | STRONG_AVOID\n221\t- `extracted_conditions` — list of conditions if any (e.g., \"if VN-Index above 1300\")\n222\t- `extracted_timeframe` — INTRADAY | DAYS | WEEKS | MONTHS | LONG_TERM\n223\t- `extraction_confidence` — how confident extractor is (separate from intent strength)\n224\t- `kol_id` — links to BC-6 KOL profile\n225\t- `published_at` — when video/post went live\n226\t\n227\tIf extraction confidence < 0.7, flag for human review before counting in calibration.\n228\t\n229\t### The Enforcement\n230\t\n231\tRecommendation aggregate validates fields. Calibration database only includes `extraction_confidence >= 0.7` records.\n232\t\n233\t---\n234\t\n235\t## Rule 10: Backtest Reproducibility\n236\t\n237\t### The Problem\n238\t\n239\tYou ran a backtest 6 months ago, got 23% return. Today you run \"the same backtest\" and get 18%. Why? Different code? Different data? You can't tell.\n240\t\n241\t### The Rule\n242\t\n243\tEvery backtest run records:\n244\t- `code_commit_hash` — full git hash of stockforge at run time\n245\t- `data_snapshot_id` — reference to DB snapshot or \"live as of date\"\n246\t- `config_file_hash` — hash of strategy config used\n247\t- `random_seed` — fixed seed\n248\t- `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`\n249\t- `result_summary` — dataclass with all key metrics\n250\t- `result_full_path` — R2 link to detailed trade log\n251\t\n252\tBacktest framework auto-records all of this. Re-running same `(commit, snapshot, config, seed)` must produce identical result.\n253\t\n254\t### The Enforcement\n255\t\n256\tBacktest engine validates inputs present before running. Output stored immutable. CI test: run same backtest twice, assert identical output.\n257\t\n258\t---\n259\t\n260\t## Quick Reference Table\n261\t\n262\t| Concern | Rule | Enforcement |\n263\t|---|---|---|\n264\t| Look-ahead in fundamentals | I-S2, Rule 1 | `get_as_of()` only |\n265\t| Survivor bias | I-S3, Rule 2 | Universe includes delisted |\n266\t| Price adjustment confusion | I-S4, Rule 3 | `adjustment_type` mandatory |\n267\t| Source disagreement | I-S5, Rule 4 | Reconciled view |\n268\t| Currency confusion | I-S6, Rule 5 | `Money` enforces currency |\n269\t| LLM hallucination | I-S1, Rule 6 | Provenance fields mandatory |\n270\t| Sentiment vagueness | Rule 7 | Categorical, not numeric |\n271\t| News lag | Rule 8 | `acting_lag` in queries |\n272\t| KOL recommendation context | Rule 9 | Conditions + timeframe required |\n273\t| Backtest reproducibility | I-S53, Rule 10 | Auto-record metadata |\n274\t\n275\t---\n276\t\n277\t## When This Protocol Conflicts With Convenience\n278\t\n279\tIt will. You'll want to query \"latest\" data for a backtest because it's faster. You'll want to skip currency tag for prototype. You'll want to dump LLM output without provenance for first version.\n280\t\n281\t**Don't.**\n282\t\n283\tThe protocol exists because every shortcut compounds. A backtest with look-ahead bias won't fail loudly — it'll just give you false confidence and you'll lose money in production.\n284\t\n285\tIf the protocol genuinely blocks legitimate work, that's a constitutional amendment discussion, not a workaround.\n286\t\n287\tLast modified: 2026-04-23 (v1.0 initial — stock-specific data integrity)\n288\t"}]},"uuid":"2dcc52b5-39cc-42a9-9817-6a85a6525c14","timestamp":"2026-04-30T14:41:57.981Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\constitution\\financial-data-protocol.md","content":"# Financial Data Protocol — StockForge\n\n> Stock-specific data integrity rules. Real money depends on these.\n> Companion to `invariants.md`. Read both before working with any data layer.\n\n## Why This Exists\n\nStock data has unique failure modes that don't exist in idea-validation or general SaaS:\n- **Look-ahead bias** — using data agent didn't have at decision time → fake \"winning\" backtest\n- **Survivorship bias** — only training on companies still trading → models that fail on real future\n- **Adjustment confusion** — comparing pre-split price to post-split → 10x errors\n- **Stale fundamentals** — using FY2023 filed in March 2024 for January 2024 decision → impossible-in-reality\n- **Currency drift** — FX changes between price update and conversion → silent value distortion\n- **Source disagreement** — vnstock vs FiinPro vs TCBS disagree → which to trust?\n\nThis protocol is the answer to each.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 1: Point-in-Time Integrity\n\n### The Problem\n\nYou query \"what was company X's P/E on 2023-06-15?\" The naive answer uses Q1 2023 EPS. But Q1 2023 was filed on 2023-04-30 — was it really known on April 30, or April 28? When did ratios get computed? Different sources have different filing dates for the same period.\n\n### The Rule\n\nEvery fundamental data record has THREE date fields:\n- `period_end` — what period this represents (e.g., 2023-03-31 for Q1 2023)\n- `filing_date` — when this was officially published\n- `ingested_at` — when our system learned about it\n\nFor backtest: filter `WHERE filing_date <= as_of_date AND ingested_at <= as_of_date`.\nFor live: filter `WHERE filing_date IS NOT NULL` (no in-progress estimates).\nFor estimates/forecasts: separate table `forecasts` with `forecast_date`, `for_period_end`, `source`.\n\n### The Enforcement\n\n`FundamentalRepository` has only two methods:\n- `get_as_of(ticker, as_of_date)` — uses point-in-time filter\n- `get_latest(ticker)` — uses today's date\n\nThere is no `get_all()` or `get_by_period()` that could be misused for backtest.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 2: Survivorship-Aware Universe Construction\n\n### The Problem\n\nIf you backtest \"buy stocks with P/E < 10 in 2018, hold 3 years\", and your dataset only includes companies still listed in 2024, you've cherry-picked survivors. Real 2018 universe included companies that later went bankrupt or got delisted.\n\n### The Rule\n\n- Universe table includes ALL stocks ever traded, with `first_traded_at`, `delisted_at`, `suspended_periods`\n- Backtest universe construction: `WHERE first_traded_at <= as_of_date AND (delisted_at IS NULL OR delisted_at > as_of_date) AND NOT in_suspension(ticker, as_of_date)`\n- Delisted stocks keep their full price history\n- \"Why delisted\" tagged: `BANKRUPTCY | MERGER | PRIVATIZATION | EXCHANGE_MIGRATION | OTHER`\n\n### The Enforcement\n\nBacktest framework `Universe.construct(as_of_date)` returns the survivor-aware universe. There is no `Universe.current_listed_only()` method available in backtest paths.\n\nCI gate checks: backtest dataset must include at least 5% delisted stocks. Less = warning that dataset is suspect.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 3: Adjustment Type Tagging\n\n### The Problem\n\nStock at 100,000 splits 1:2 → next day at 50,000. If you look at raw historical data, looks like 50% loss. Adjusted data smooths this out, but mixing adjusted (for chart) with unadjusted (for transaction calculation) gives 10x errors.\n\n### The Rule\n\nEvery price record has `adjustment_type`:\n- `NONE` — raw historical (what you actually paid)\n- `DIVIDEND` — adjusted for dividends only\n- `SPLIT` — adjusted for splits only\n- `BOTH` — fully adjusted (typical for charts/return calc)\n\n`Quote` value object has `adjustment_type` field. Repository methods are explicit:\n- `get_quotes_adjusted(ticker, range)` → returns BOTH\n- `get_quotes_raw(ticker, range)` → returns NONE\n- No mixed query allowed.\n\n### The Enforcement\n\nQuote dataclass enforces `adjustment_type` not None. Mixing in same calculation raises `MixedAdjustmentError`.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 4: Source Attribution & Reconciliation\n\n### The Problem\n\nvnstock says HPG Q3 2024 revenue = 35,000 tỷ. FiinPro says 35,200 tỷ. TCBS says 34,800 tỷ. Which is \"true\"?\n\n### The Rule\n\n- Every data point stores `source_provider` (enum: VNSTOCK | FIINPRO | TCBS | SSI | MANUAL | SCRAPED_<source>)\n- \"Truth\" view materialized via reconciliation rules:\n  - If only one source: that's the truth\n  - If sources agree (within 1% tolerance): truth = average, confidence = HIGH\n  - If sources disagree (>1%): truth = manual override OR flag for review, confidence = LOW\n  - Manual override always wins, with `override_reason` documented\n- UI shows truth value + \"X of Y sources confirm\" badge\n\n### The Enforcement\n\n`ReconciledFundamental` view in DB. Application layer queries reconciled view by default. Raw single-source queries explicitly via `RawFundamentalRepository` for debugging only.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 5: Currency Discipline\n\n### The Problem\n\nVND fundamentals + USD foreign comparable + EUR debt instrument = silent type confusion if not strict.\n\n### The Rule\n\n- `Money` value object always has `currency` field (default VND for domestic data)\n- Cross-currency math requires explicit `convert(target_currency, as_of_rate)` call\n- FX rates stored with `as_of_date` (point-in-time integrity applies)\n- No implicit conversion — `Money(100, USD) + Money(2_000_000, VND)` raises `CurrencyMismatchError`\n\n### The Enforcement\n\n`Money` dataclass `__add__`, `__sub__`, `__mul__` validate currency. CI test verifies no implicit conversion possible.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 6: LLM Output Provenance\n\n### The Problem\n\nLLM extracts \"HPG announced 30% dividend increase\" from a news article. Two months later, you wonder: was that real or hallucinated?\n\n### The Rule\n\nEvery LLM-extracted claim record has:\n- `source_url` — where extracted from (URL or file path)\n- `source_text_excerpt` — exact text quoted (≤500 chars)\n- `extractor_model` — model name + version (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\")\n- `extractor_prompt_hash` — hash of system prompt used (for reproducibility)\n- `extractor_version` — code version (commit hash)\n- `extracted_at` — timestamp\n- `confidence_extracted` — LLM's stated confidence in the extraction (0-1)\n- `verified_by_human` — bool (default false)\n\nWithout all these fields, claim cannot be inserted to DB.\n\n### The Enforcement\n\nRepository constructor validates all fields. Schema NOT NULL constraints. Verifier agent randomly samples 5% of new claims for human review queue.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 7: Sentiment Score Calibration\n\n### The Problem\n\nLLM says \"this article is 80% bullish\". What does 80% mean? Is it calibrated to anything?\n\n### The Rule\n\nSentiment scores are categorical, not numeric:\n- `STRONGLY_BULLISH | BULLISH | NEUTRAL | BEARISH | STRONGLY_BEARISH`\n\nPlus extracted features:\n- `mentioned_tickers: list[Ticker]`\n- `key_phrases: list[str]`\n- `tone_indicators: list[str]` (e.g., \"uses superlatives\", \"compares to leader\", \"raises concern\")\n\nAggregation to \"sentiment score\" happens in code, not LLM:\n- e.g., `sentiment_score = (bullish_count - bearish_count) / total_count` over a time window\n\n### The Enforcement\n\nSentiment LLM tasks return enum, not number. Application layer converts to score with explicit formula. Backtest can validate which scoring formula correlates with subsequent price moves.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 8: Anti-Look-Ahead in News & Sentiment\n\n### The Problem\n\nYou backtest \"buy stocks with positive news momentum\". But the news article from Jan 15 might have been published 8pm — too late to act. Or the sentiment was scored 3 days later when more context was available.\n\n### The Rule\n\nEvery news/sentiment record has:\n- `published_at` — when source published it (best estimate)\n- `ingested_at` — when our system saw it\n- `scored_at` — when sentiment was computed\n\nBacktest filters: `WHERE published_at <= as_of_date AND scored_at <= as_of_date AND published_at + acting_lag <= action_date`\n\nWhere `acting_lag` = realistic time between news and possible trade (e.g., next day open if published after market close).\n\n### The Enforcement\n\nNews/sentiment repository has only `get_known_as_of(ticker, as_of_date)` method for backtest. The lag is enforced in the query.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 9: KOL Recommendation Provenance\n\n### The Problem\n\nKOL says \"buy HPG\" in a 30-minute video. When exactly? Was it part of a long disclaimer? Was it conditional (\"if breaks 30k then buy\")?\n\n### The Rule\n\nExtracted KOL recommendations include:\n- `source_url` — full video/post URL\n- `timestamp_in_source` — for video: timestamp range (e.g., \"12:34-13:02\")\n- `transcript_excerpt` — exact text quoted\n- `extracted_intent` — categorical: STRONG_BUY | BUY | WATCH | NEUTRAL | AVOID | STRONG_AVOID\n- `extracted_conditions` — list of conditions if any (e.g., \"if VN-Index above 1300\")\n- `extracted_timeframe` — INTRADAY | DAYS | WEEKS | MONTHS | LONG_TERM\n- `extraction_confidence` — how confident extractor is (separate from intent strength)\n- `kol_id` — links to BC-6 KOL profile\n- `published_at` — when video/post went live\n\nIf extraction confidence < 0.7, flag for human review before counting in calibration.\n\n### The Enforcement\n\nRecommendation aggregate validates fields. Calibration database only includes `extraction_confidence >= 0.7` records.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 10: Backtest Reproducibility\n\n### The Problem\n\nYou ran a backtest 6 months ago, got 23% return. Today you run \"the same backtest\" and get 18%. Why? Different code? Different data? You can't tell.\n\n### The Rule\n\nEvery backtest run records:\n- `code_commit_hash` — full git hash of stockforge at run time\n- `data_snapshot_id` — reference to DB snapshot or \"live as of date\"\n- `config_file_hash` — hash of strategy config used\n- `random_seed` — fixed seed\n- `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`\n- `result_summary` — dataclass with all key metrics\n- `result_full_path` — R2 link to detailed trade log\n\nBacktest framework auto-records all of this. Re-running same `(commit, snapshot, config, seed)` must produce identical result.\n\n### The Enforcement\n\nBacktest engine validates inputs present before running. Output stored immutable. CI test: run same backtest twice, assert identical output.\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference Table\n\n| Concern | Rule | Enforcement |\n|---|---|---|\n| Look-ahead in fundamentals | I-S2, Rule 1 | `get_as_of()` only |\n| Survivor bias | I-S3, Rule 2 | Universe includes delisted |\n| Price adjustment confusion | I-S4, Rule 3 | `adjustment_type` mandatory |\n| Source disagreement | I-S5, Rule 4 | Reconciled view |\n| Currency confusion | I-S6, Rule 5 | `Money` enforces currency |\n| LLM hallucination | I-S1, Rule 6 | Provenance fields mandatory |\n| Sentiment vagueness | Rule 7 | Categorical, not numeric |\n| News lag | Rule 8 | `acting_lag` in queries |\n| KOL recommendation context | Rule 9 | Conditions + timeframe required |\n| Backtest reproducibility | I-S53, Rule 10 | Auto-record metadata |\n\n---\n\n## When This Protocol Conflicts With Convenience\n\nIt will. You'll want to query \"latest\" data for a backtest because it's faster. You'll want to skip currency tag for prototype. You'll want to dump LLM output without provenance for first version.\n\n**Don't.**\n\nThe protocol exists because every shortcut compounds. A backtest with look-ahead bias won't fail loudly — it'll just give you false confidence and you'll lose money in production.\n\nIf the protocol genuinely blocks legitimate work, that's a constitutional amendment discussion, not a workaround.\n\nLast modified: 2026-04-23 (v1.0 initial — stock-specific data integrity)\n","numLines":288,"startLine":1,"totalLines":288}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"54a3615e-06c7-4bd1-8823-15ab67cf8f5e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"26da415a-76e5-4042-8420-5582125d8a7d","version":"2.1.123","gitBranch":"main"}
